status_summary: PPO operates as a central clearance point for political staffing. Bloomberg reported on 2025-03-06 that PPO, then led by Sergio Gor, asked candidates loyalty questions and reviewed donations and social media; an OPM memo of 2025-04-10 on Schedule C terms of employment flexibilities, signed by Acting Director Charles Ezell, says approving or withdrawing an agency's Schedule C appointing authority requires preclearance from the White House Office of Presidential Personnel, in addition to approval by OPM's White House Liaison; and OPM's Schedule G guidance (2025-07-29) gives PPO final review of agency requests. Dan Scavino was named in August 2025 to succeed Gor, and an August 2026 Breitbart piece quotes cabinet members praising PPO and relays White House figures of 591 civilian nominees confirmed in the 119th Congress. Independent measures are weaker: Brookings counted 216 confirmations at day 300 (against roughly 700 positions in the 15 departments) and Partnership for Public Service data showing the fewest nominations in a first 300 days since Reagan, and a July 2026 analysis reported a record pace of departures among confirmed officials and more acting officials. Agency hiring generally runs through agency strategic hiring committees under EO 14356 (2025-10-15), which names no PPO role, and the order moving positions into Schedule Policy/Career (EO 14410, signed 2026-06-03) assigns recommendation and rulemaking roles to OPM and does not mention PPO. The Mandate itself notes that departments and agencies hold direct legal authority over hiring and firing; PPO's documented clearance role covers Schedule C and Schedule G appointments and nominee vetting, while its role in firings of political appointees and in choosing Schedule Policy/Career positions was not documented.

timeline.event: Bloomberg (via Fortune) reports PPO under Sergio Gor put candidates through loyalty questions and reviewed donations and social media, with a White House official saying more than 200 nominees had gone to the Senate and more than 1,300 vacancies had been filled.

OPM Acting Director Charles Ezell issues a memo to agency heads, Schedule C Terms of Employment Flexibilities, which says approving or withdrawing an agency's Schedule C appointing authority requires preclearance from the White House Office of Presidential Personnel (routed through the agency's White House Liaison) in addition to approval by OPM's White House Liaison, and that Schedule C appointments should not advance without coordinating with the agency White House Liaison.

Eight senators write to the acting OPM director asking for written information on PPO's role in hiring Schedule C appointees; they say the April memo encouraged higher salaries and a bypass of standard hiring review, which they argue would let appointees start without vetting.
OPM issues Schedule G guidance routing agency requests through OPM's Executive and Schedule C System with final review and approval by the White House Office of Presidential Personnel.

The Associated Press reports that Trump will install deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino to lead PPO in place of Sergio Gor, whom he had nominated as ambassador to India; no effective date is given. Brookings (2025-11-24) later reports Scavino as Gor's successor.

EO 14356 requires each agency to set up a strategic hiring committee (deputy head, chief of staff and designees) to approve filling each vacancy, with notice to OPM; it exempts Schedule C, Schedule G and presidentially appointed positions and names no PPO role.

Brookings reports 216 Senate confirmations at day 300 against roughly 700 positions in the 15 departments and a record 53 withdrawn nominations, cites Partnership for Public Service data showing the fewest nominations in a first 300 days since Reagan, and describes the Senate's 2025-09-11 rule change allowing batch confirmations (batches of 41 on 2025-09-18 and 74 on 2025-10-07).
OPM publishes the final rule letting agencies move policy-influencing positions into Schedule Policy/Career (effective 2026-03-09); agencies petition OPM, which recommends positions to the President.

EO 14410 (published 2026-06-10) places the positions listed in its appendix into Schedule Policy/Career and lets agency heads petition the OPM Director to recommend additional positions to the President; the text read does not mention PPO.

A Partnership for Public Service analysis, reported by Government Executive, finds 27 Senate-confirmed officials (11.4 percent) have left, a record pace, and the fewest nominations of any president since Reagan, with more acting officials; the article does not name PPO.

Breitbart publishes an exclusive in which cabinet officials praise PPO under Scavino and White House-provided figures are cited, including 591 civilian nominees confirmed in the 119th Congress; the figures are not independently verified and no critics are quoted.

title: Run political staffing through a strong Presidential Personnel Office
uncertainties: The OPM Schedule C memo (dated 2025-04-10) was read on opm.gov; the Schedule G guidance was read as an OPM release, not as the underlying guidance document. The March 2025 vetting description and figures rest on a Bloomberg article that relies on unnamed people and a White House official. The Breitbart piece is a favorable account built on White House-provided figures and statements from officials, not independently verified. The Scavino handover date is not established: the AP report of 2025-08-26 says he will take over and Brookings later reports him as Gor's successor. Whether PPO has a role in choosing the positions placed in Schedule Policy/Career is not shown by the text of EO 14410 (an unofficial rendition of the text was read; the appendix was not). Overlap with c03-01 and c03-07 (Schedule Policy/Career) is intended; this record tracks only PPO's role. The progress figure of 55 is a judgment: PPO's clearance role is documented, but its authority over firings and over agency hiring generally is not.
